narrative.overview: Brownie Water Tracker combines the clarity of a practical wellness tool with the companionship of a small illustrated world. Warm paper, a visible grid, ink outlines, and compact Lato typography keep information trustworthy; animated mascots and turquoise water keep it friendly.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, gridded canvas with clean white surfaces and ink-black structure
Friendly illustrated mascots used as product companions, never decoration alone
Turquoise water as the signature environmental motif
Green and coral reserved for meaningful positive and caution states
Compact, bold Lato hierarchy with plain-spoken, reassuring copy
Light and dark themes that retain the same hierarchy and semantic color roles

rules.name: The Ink-First Rule
rules.body: Primary actions and structural borders use ink; Pool Blue belongs to the water world, not every control.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Use Lato for every interface role. Hierarchy comes from weight, scale, spacing, and case—not a second display face.

rules.name: The Mobile-Reflow Rule
rules.body: Recompose, do not merely shrink: floating objects enter normal flow, paired layouts stack, and essential actions become full width only when space demands it.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface participates in normal document flow, prefer an ink border over a shadow.

rules.name: The Pill-for-Actions Rule
rules.body: Filled and outlined calls to action are pills; content containers are not.

dos: Do preserve the warm canvas, visible 32px grid, ink outlines, and white surfaces as the system's default field.
Do use mascots to demonstrate companionship, progress, or product behavior.
Do reserve shadows for elements that overlap or temporarily float above the page.
donts: Don't turn Pool Blue, green, or coral into general-purpose decoration across ordinary controls.
Don't add gradients, glassmorphism, blurred panels, or glossy app-store styling.
Don't animate continuously without viewport pausing, a user control, and a reduced-motion fallback.
